newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Q4 aluminium premiums set at $65.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Q4 aluminium premiums set at $65.

text.p: South Korea's aluminium import premiums for the fourth quarter were set at around $65 per tonne from $70-$75 in the third quarter, traders said on Tuesday.
The price is based on the London Metal Exchange's (LME) cash price on CIF Pusan.

In Japan, traders said aluminium import premiums for the fourth quarter were set at $62 a tonne above LME cash prices on a CIF basis at the end of August. The premiums for Japanese importers had been a benchmark for South Korean buyers.

"Up to now, the Korean premium had been about $10 above Japan's level. But the fourth quarter premium gap narrowed to $3 as our aluminium demands for the fourth quarter are seen shrinking," a trader with Samsung Corp said.
"Foreign sellers demanded a premium of $70 for the fourth quarter when we started negotiations late August, while local buyers asked for less than $65," a trader at Ssangyong Corp said.
They said a slowdown in the domestic economy and the sharp depreciation of the won against the dollar had put pressure on demand for the fourth quarter.
"Import premiums for the fourth quarter shipment fell to around $65 because of lower demands and the weaker won," a trader at a major trading house said.
Metal importers suffered large foreign exchange losses, weakening buying interest, he said.

Traders said demand was also affected by a slowdown in purchases by Aluminium of Korea Co Ltd, a unit of the Hyundai Group, Aluminium of Korea, usually a large buyer of the metal, had a large surplus of aluminium ingot which had piled up during a 24-day strike at its Ulsan plant in mid-July.
Aluminium stocks at Pusan, a major metal arrival port, were near their bottom against 25,000 tonnes in mid-May, a senior official of a Pusan-based warehouse firm said.

"Local distributors used to stockpile the metal at warehouses before selling it to end-users. But it has changed now. They import the metal only after completing sales contracts to save carrying costs," the warehouse official said. He expected this trend to last until next March.
South Korea's aluminium imports in 1995 totalled 835,784 tonnes including 610,691 tonnes of primary ingot and 101,012 tonnes of billet.
